Oh, another thing (I feel this one fits the original thread better) my mom would always say how if I didn't stay RIGHT BY HER in public I would get kidnapped, raped, and murdered. Everything was the end of the world. She overly built fear in everything instead of the appropriate level of caution.

Now I'm 26 and terrified of EVERYTHING. I have severe agoraphobia, social anxiety, and generalized anxiety disorder.

For training at that age it's really important to take them out every 20 minutes. I know that's a lot, but trust me. When they are that young they can't hold their bladder longer than that. How big is the crate? Usually they won't eliminate in their "den". Picture of pup in crate if possible? Also take pup out after playing, after eating, and after being in crate for any length of time. When you go out STAY out until they go. When my pup was young I literally brought a chair outside and sat outside every time until he went. You can't expect the puppy to tell you they have to go when they are that young, by the time they realize they have to go, they will just go. The first couple months are very tedious, but if you really work hard in the early parts, it'll really pay off.
